degree: Diplôme Arts et Techniques du Théâtre conférant le grade de Master

whatYouStudy: Three years covering physical acoustics, sound technologies and practices, and the aesthetics of artistic projects, training students for 'régie, ingénierie ou création' roles as 'l'interlocuteur privilégié' providing both technical and artistic guidance on a production. A master-level mémoire is written (the prerequisites explicitly ask for 'qualités rédactionnelles (en vue de la rédaction d'un mémoire de niveau Master)'). Cross-disciplinary work with the other nine ENSATT parcours (jeu, mise en scène, scénographie, conception lumière, direction technique, écriture dramatique…) and with CNSMD Lyon. entryRequirements: Minimum age 18 at 1 September of the entry year, no dérogation. All candidates must hold the baccalauréat (or an equivalence) AND 'justifier d'au moins 2 années d'études supérieures et être détenteurs de 120 crédits ECTS ... délivrés dans le cadre d'une formation reconnue par l'État'. Three recommended books: Daniel Deshays 'Pour une écriture du son'; Larrue & Mervant-Roux 'Le son du théâtre XIXe-XXIe siècle'; Yann Paranthoën 'Propos d'un tailleur de sons'.
portfolioSpec: Admissibilité 1 = 'Dossier de recherche : projet de réalisation sonore sur un thème donné'. OU le portrait sonore d'une promenade nocturne que vous avez effectuée' — the sequence must remain comprehensible to the listener. Deliverables: (1) a sound document not exceeding 3 minutes in WAV or AIFF ('format compressé refusé'), where 'la réalisation sera structurée par la prise de son, le montage et le mixage effectués avec les moyens dont dispose le/la candidat(e), MÊME RUDIMENTAIRES'; (2) a PDF text justifying the reflection, conception and realisation, not exceeding 6 typed A4 pages. Both uploaded via francetransfert.numerique.gouv.fr to concours@ensatt.fr, files named CONCOURS_NAME_INITIAL_REGISTRATIONNUMBER.
auditionSpec: Admissibilité 2 (on site at ENSATT, Lyon): a written physics paper (2h00, coefficient 1) and a written paper analysing texts and/or audiovisual documents (1h30, coefficient 1). Style exercises additionally required: one fugue in the style of J. S. program: Biennio Accademico di II livello in Music Production (Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Music Production)
university: Saint Louis College of Music (AFAM institution authorised by MUR)
institutionType: Private specialist music academy, ministerially authorised (AFAM) — degrees recognised by the Italian MUR
durationEcts: 2 years; approx. 300 contact hours per year. CFA total UNVERIFIED (the standard is 120 CFA for an Italian biennio).
language: Italian and English (the course page states "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese")
focus: Music Production — the closest thing in this slice to a producer's degree
whatYouStudy: Verified from the official page. Each student learns to run a music-production project through every phase, from the creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. Named modules: LABORATORIO DI PRODUZIONE — developing original projects with a music-producer's approach to the whole production chain; TECNICHE DI RIPRESA E REGISTRAZIONE — each specialising student produces TWO TRACKS end-to-end, from pre-production and arrangement through rehearsals, recording and overdubbing, microphone choice and placement, editing, mixing and mastering; ORCHESTRAZIONE — professional virtual orchestration, arrangement, real and virtual instruments, sound construction within the production; ANALISI DELLA PRODUZIONE MUSICALE — evolution of the producer's role, the approaches of the most influential producers in history, and the compositional/structural/expressive techniques of the main contemporary popular-music languages, completed with sound design applied to the timbral character of a track; DIRITTO D'AUTORE, ROYALTIES E CONTRATTUALISTICA — copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts. The bienni are explicitly "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", built around each student's own artistic direction, with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the whole degree.
entryRequirements: Stated requirement: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio" (conditional enrolment possible). portfolioSpec: VERIFIED and exact for the pre-selection stage: "Registra uno o più video contenenti 3 brani, eseguiti da te in gruppo (minimo trio) che siano rappresentativi della tua attività artistica" — record one or more videos containing THREE PIECES, performed by you in a group of at least a TRIO, representative of your artistic activity; files must be uploaded to YouTube or a similar web portal and the LINKS entered in the application form. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this ensemble-video wording is the shared text used across Saint Louis's academic courses and is clearly written for performer tracks — for the Music Production biennio you should ask the Segreteria in writing what the equivalent production portfolio is (most likely produced/mixed tracks rather than a live trio video). Also mandatory: download and check the Piano di studi, which lists the competences tested in each individual prova.
auditionSpec: Two-stage: (1) pre-selection on the submitted video links; (2) for those who pass, admission tests held ON SITE in Rome over TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS, in the June and September sessions. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year, drawn from Saint Louis's own first-level graduates plus external candidates selected by audition.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — this is the weak point. The published requirement names a "diploma accademico triennale di primo livello" (an Italian first-level academic diploma in music). Italian law generally allows a university laurea to serve as the entry title for a biennio, and Saint Louis runs an international students office, but the page does NOT say so. stipend: LAZIODISCO contributions reported at roughly EUR 1,900–5,000 per year of study. UNVERIFIED against the official 2027 bando.

program: Creative Production (Music) MA
university: Catalyst – Institute for Creative Arts and Technology, Berlin (degree validated by Plymouth Marjon University, UK)
institutionType: Private specialist creative-arts institute, not a German state Hochschule. Its own FAQ describes it as a registered training centre regulated under German law whose degrees are 'validated by our accrediting partner Plymouth Marjon University in the United Kingdom', with MA graduates receiving 'British degrees and certificates with an equivalent status recognised in Germany and the EU'. The earlier description 'state-accredited HEI' overstates this — correct it.
degree: MA (Master of Arts), awarded by Plymouth Marjon University (UK)
durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. Credit total (UK credits or ECTS) is NOT published on the course page or fees page — it sits in the downloadable course guide/syllabus. UNVERIFIED.
language: English throughout — 'taught entirely in English'. No German required.
focus: Sonic Arts / practice-led artistic research, spanning music production, electronic and electroacoustic music, spatial and immersive audio, creative coding, sound art
whatYouStudy: Five modules forming one arc: Imagine (detailed research proposal, research contract and work plan agreed with a supervisor), Contextualise (critical review of existing concepts, literature, practices and methods in the field), Investigate (survey then depth), Present (creation, public presentation and documentation of outward-facing work), Synthesise (a substantial original work or body of works). Three concurrent year-long workshops: Creative Sound Practices — weekly sessions moving 'between modular synthesis, spatial sound, creative coding, field recording, improvisation and sound installation', with the explicit aim being 'not technical mastery but the development of a personal methodology'; Contexts of Listening (musicology, sound studies, philosophy, critical theory — Oliveros, Schaeffer, Attali, Fisher, Butler, Derrida and others); and Supervision (one-to-one plus group critique). Guest artists have included Nicolas Collins, Bob Ostertag and Kaffe Matthews. The page is emphatic and repeats the warning twice: 'This is not a studio engineering degree, a vocational production course or a genre-based music programme. It is postgraduate artistic research' and 'This programme is not suited to those seeking vocational production training, DAW certification or a genre-based music course.' Encouragingly for him, past students have come 'from various backgrounds, including songwriting, house, techno, folk, jazz ... experimental and electroacoustic music'.
entryRequirements: 'Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, with an Honours grade (e.g. 2:1 in the UK university system) or be in the final year of studies for one.' Non-standard entry exists: applicants lacking the minimum education requirement 'may be assessed on the strength of a professional CV and portfolio, which must demonstrate a solid background in artistic practice and research'. English at 'IELTS 6 (referred to as B2 in Germany and other EU countries)', evidenced either by an official certificate or by taking Catalyst's own online assessment — which is a real advantage given he has not sat IELTS. Submission is via an online portal: transcripts, portfolio with work samples, professional references, and a project proposal.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — likely yes, but not stated as such. The requirement is a bachelor's 'in a relevant discipline' at Honours level, and students are said to come 'from a wide range of backgrounds'. Software engineering is arguably relevant to creative coding and spatial audio, and the non-standard route offers a fallback, but the page does not name computer science and selection turns on the project proposal and portfolio. Ask Admissions directly whether an SE BSc satisfies 'relevant discipline'; the FAQ invites exactly that conversation.
portfolioSpec: Not quantified anywhere public — UNVERIFIED as to number and duration. Confirmed components: a portfolio with work samples; a detailed project proposal framed as practice-led artistic research (the school runs free online prep workshops on artistic and practice-based research specifically to help applicants shape it, and offers to send a recent graduate's final project portfolio as a reference on request); a sample of research/academic writing; academic transcripts; professional references; and personal/educational documentation. The proposal, not the music, is the decisive artefact.
auditionSpec: None — confirmed: there is no interview or audition requirement; the assessment is a digital submission reviewed by admissions. A voluntary call with the Admissions team is offered and, given the 'relevant discipline' question, he should take it.

For a September 2027 start expect the same pattern — priority around late February 2027 and a visa-required deadline around 30 April 2027 — but the 2027 dates are not yet published. Plus a non-refundable enrolment fee of €895 per study year, which includes visa support. So roughly €12,588 for the full-time year, or about €16,000 over two years part-time. The programme is embedded in Berlin's experimental scene, engaging each year with Atonal, CTM, Floating University and MANIFEST:IO, running a public two-day MA Symposium and the student-run Etikett Radio (with partnerships including Refuge Worldwide). program: Master of Music – Elektronische Komposition (Electronic Composition)
university: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)
institutionType: Public conservatory (Musikhochschule) — one of Europe's largest music academies; the 'largest' claim is marketing, not verified here
durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years) / 120 credits — confirmed on the official programme page
language: German. Applicants who did not graduate from a German-speaking institution must prove German 'min. level A2 according to the European Framework of Reference' — an unusually low bar, but teaching and the colloquium are in German.

whatYouStudy: Independent compositional work and professionalisation: mixed instrumental/electronic composition, installations and internet works, self-organised concerts of student work. The electronic and instrumental composition classes cooperate closely, so students may join the other class's projects and take main-subject lessons there. All practical work happens in the Studio für Elektronische Musik. CONFIRMED on the official page. Note the aptitude exam explicitly tests knowledge of 'Literatur und Satztechniken der zeitgenössischen elektronischen und auch instrumentalen Musik' — i.e. contemporary art-music repertoire and compositional technique. No DJing, no club-music production, no mixing/mastering curriculum.
entryRequirements: Official page: 'Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent. Admission to the electronic composition program is also possible with an undergraduate degree in instrumental composition.' The binding Eignungsprüfungsordnung annex (09.12.2025) is stricter and names the required bachelor as: 'Studiengang Elektronische Komposition oder Studiengang Instrumentale Komposition'. Plus German A2 minimum, application via muvac, €50 admission-procedure fee. The exam also requires proof of 'grundlegende Computerkenntnisse und Basiswissen in Musikelektronik' (basic computer skills and basic knowledge of music electronics).
acceptsNonMusic: No, other than as a rare exception — CONFIRMED in the binding regulations: 'Nur in Ausnahmefällen, bei außerordentlicher Begabung und Vorbildung kann ein Bachelorabschluss aus anderen Kunst- oder aus Informatikbereichen akzeptiert werden.' ('Only in exceptional cases, given extraordinary talent and prior education, can a bachelor's degree from other art or computer-science fields be accepted.') Computer science is named, but only as an exception route conditional on demonstrated extraordinary talent — not a normal pathway for a software-engineering graduate with no music training.
portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the Eignungsprüfungsordnung annex, Anhang §5, 09.12.2025 — the programme page itself does not state it): 'Vorauswahl (digital) – Arbeitsproben: Erwartet werden Dokumentationen oder Produktionen von mindestens drei Kompositionen, welche ganz oder teilweise mit elektronischen Medien erstellt wurden, ggf. mit Partituren als PDF. Jede einzelne Arbeit muss mit Titel, Genre, Besetzung und Namen der Komponistin/des Komponisten versehen sein.' So: at least THREE compositions created wholly or partly with electronic media, documentation or production files, scores as PDF where applicable, each labelled with title, genre, instrumentation and composer name. No duration limit is published. Upload via muvac.
auditionSpec: No instrumental audition. Digital pre-selection on the work samples, then a main-subject examination: 'Die Hauptfachprüfung besteht aus einem Kolloquium mit der Vorstellung und Diskussion weiterer auf Anforderung eingereichter Werke, mit anspruchsvollen Fragen zur eigenen musikalischen Ästhetik und zur Kenntnis von Literatur und Satztechniken der zeitgenössischen elektronischen und auch instrumentalen Musik. Es sind grundlegende Computerkenntnisse und Basiswissen in Musikelektronik nachzuweisen.' Note 'anspruchsvolle Fragen' (demanding questions) and that FURTHER works may be requested. entryRequirements: CRITICAL CORRECTION — the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page states: 'Voraussetzung ist der Nachweis eines abgeschlossenen künstlerischen Bachelor- oder Diplomstudiums oder eines gleichwertig anerkannten künstlerischen Studiengangs mit Schwerpunktsetzung im Bereich Musikproduktion (z.B. acceptsNonMusic: No — this is a hard correction to the earlier 'Check'. The requirement is not merely 'a bachelor's degree': it must be an artistic bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis, and the examples given are Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's own Ton und Bild bachelor. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither artistic nor production-focused in the sense meant, so he is formally ineligible, before the audition is even considered.
portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page). Jazz/Pop major pre-selection: a portfolio of FOUR TO SIX already-realised works (or excerpts) in different styles from the jazz/popular-music production field; one audio file/track package per work sample; TOTAL DURATION 15–20 MINUTES; accepted formats stereo, 5.1/7.1 or Atmos; stereo mixes as stereo .wav, multichannel as clearly labelled mono .wav files (5.1/7.1) or as an ADM file (Atmos); each work sample accompanied by a short description of how it was made. PLUS unedited videos of the applicant's own artistic performance on instrument/voice (jazz/pop) with improvisation or ad-libs, tempi and styles varying, own composition allowed, max 20 minutes total — with an important alternative for keyboard/jazz piano: 'die Einreichung von bis zu drei Stücken mit Improvisation mit Hilfe von elektronischen Instrumenten wie Keyboards, Synthesizern, DAWs (z.B. Ableton live) mit deutlich erkennbarem spielerisch-handwerklichem Anteil sowie erkennbar eigener Soundgestaltung' (up to three pieces with improvisation using keyboards, synths or DAWs such as Ableton Live, with clearly recognisable playing craft and own sound design). PLUS a motivation letter referencing the chosen major and a CV with certificates. (Classical major differs: 5–6 works, 30–45 minutes, plus three works from different stylistic periods on video.)
auditionSpec: Yes — a substantial ON-SITE examination (Präsenzprüfung) in Düsseldorf, in four parts: (1) artistic presentation on instrument or voice with the same repertoire as the pre-selection, plus a prepared solo transcription (or a short a cappella piece for jazz/pop voice) AND sight-reading / sight-singing; six copies of the scores or lead sheets must be brought. (2) An UNPREPARED practical task in the chosen major, e.g. a mix or an edit, typically one to two hours. (3) Written examinations of both musical and technical hearing: musical ear (~40 min: dictations from piano and from recordings, intonation hearing, error detection, short aural analysis, instrumentation hearing) and technical ear (~40 min: listening examples including technical artefacts, level judgement, formant hearing).
